newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's opposition denounce U.S. strike on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's opposition denounce U.S. strike on Iraq.

text.p: Jordan's Islamist-led opposition deputies, in a show of solidarity, met the Iraqi envoy on Tuesday to denounce the U.S. cruise missile attack on Baghdad.

"There is nothing in the Security Council resolutions and U.N. decisions that says Iraq cannot defend its own land...I think its a petty election game," parliamentary deputy Toujan Faisal told reporters outside the Iraqi embassy in Amman.
U.S. presidential elections will take place in November.

He said a group representing opposition deputies comprising a coalition of leftwing, pan-Arabist and Islamist groups told Iraqi ambassador Nouri el-Wayess that the "Jordanian poeple stood by the Iraqi people against the U.S. aggression."
A separate statement issued by the opposition denounced the attacks against Iraqi targets and said they aimed at the unity of Iraq and its territorial intergrity.
"This attack is an attack on international legality and the independence of Iraq and a direct threat to all states in the region," the statement added.
The opposition coalition said the "blatant military intervention was aimed at engulfing the region as a whole in a sea of aggressive American imperialist wars."
